messages:
amy_support: FYI customer (NimbusHealth) flagged a behavioral regresssion after our defaults rollout yesterday. Their summaries went very terse and factual, used to be more conversational. They attached before/after examples and a repro. Escalation to their platform lead.

matt_eng: thanks — can you paste the exact request they sent? sampling params maybe different at runtime?

amy_support: here's the curl they used (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-***' -d '{"model":"open-a-lite-1","input":"Summarize the following...","max_tokens":180}'
```
They say they never set temperature/top_p explicitly. Old behavior was warm/creative. New outputs are very conservative.

june_sre: @matt_eng @carlos_research tagging SRE in case it's a rollout flag. SRE bot shows the config change was deployed 2024-11-03 02:12UTC: sampling.default.temperature=0.0, sampling.default.top_p=0.7 -> earlier it was temp=0.8/top_p=0.95 for hosted endpoints.

sre-bot: deploy:conf-3812 applied to hosted-configs region-us-east-1 by ops_lead at 1709540772.

matt_eng: that lines up. We had a PR that normalizes missing sampling values to the new defaults to improve determinism for evals. Looks like it got broadened to all customers. Not good.

carlos_research: can we confirm whether customer code relied on implicit defaults? If their requests omitted temp/top_p and our SDK used to insert 0.8/0.95, reverting might restore expected behavior.

amy_support: they confirm they never set them and relied on previous behavior. They've got automated scoring that broke. They're asking for an immediate mitigation and a rollback if possible.

matt_eng: mitigation options: 1) hotfix to scoped-configs so hosted default remains legacy for existing tenants, 2) add a tenant-specific override tier so we don't change behavior mid-flight, 3) tell customer to set explicit sampling params (not ideal). I can prepare #1 and #2, need SRE to apply rollback or scoped rollout.

june_sre: I can do a scoped rollback to region-us-east-1 for the hosted plane. ETA 30m if approved. Need a revert commit and PR link. @ops_lead can you approve emergency revert?

ops_lead: approve. ops will coordinate the rollback. Please include a note in the incident tracker and a migration plan so future PRs don't affect existing tenant defaults.

matt_eng: creating PR to pin legacy defaults to tenant configs and add an explicit flag for opt-in to deterministic eval defaults. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/patches/824. Will include tests to ensure missing sampling keys are honored per-tenant.

carlos_research: for long-term we should add an SDK-level explicit default and document it in Breaking Changes section. Also run A/B on a handful of customers before sweeping changes.

amy_support: customer update sent: "We found the issue — engineering is rolling back a defaults change. We'll follow up with a timeline and a targeted fix. Apologies for the disruption." They asked for a rollback ETA.

june_sre: rollback started 1854321160, completed 1854321265. Validation: run against their sample payloads, outputs match previous baseline.

amy_support: customer confirmed restored behavior and is un-escalating. They want a postmortem and a changelog entry before we make any other defaults changes.

matt_eng: agreed. I'll draft a short postmortem and include steps: code review checklist for default changes, tenant-impact test harness, and SDK docs.

amy_support: tagging for follow-up: @carlos_research to own postmortem, @matt_eng to own code change, @june_sre to own rollback runbook. Closing thread once PM notes are attached.

sre-bot: incident:defaults-drift-185432 - severity:high - status:resolved
